events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.50)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (Hougang Mall → Changi Airport T3, total charged $42.25, F7), so a non-exempt off-route segment would feed directly into the fare and be refundable under RD-2 [F7][RD-2]. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists (F3, 21:58–22:05, 4.04 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.90 km, +2.13 km, up to 1209 m off route) and that no RD-4(a) incident supports it: the only traffic records are speed bands (F12 Tampines Expressway band 2 21:33–21:58; F13 Punggol Road band 4; F14 Airport Boulevard band 5) and F15 records no incidents, so RD-4 does not exempt the segment [F3][F12][F15][RD-4].

The open element is consent scope under RD-5. Read in context, the chat is not a general "whichever way is faster" authorisation: the driver asked a specific routing question — “Jam on Tampines Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Tampines Avenue 7?” (F8, 21:55) — and the rider replied specifically, “可以，走 Tampines Avenue 7 吧” (F9, 21:56). The rider's agreement is on its face a SPECIFIC named-road authorisation limited to Tampines Avenue 7, and it was sent before the segment started at 21:58, so a wording that covers the segment exists [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. But RD-5 requires the record to tie the segment to the named road: a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, or a road name in a fact. Nothing does — the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, and the off-route measurement (up to 1209 m from the optimal route) does not itself say which road was used [F3][F9][RD-5]. Timing alone cannot supply the tie (G13). Nothing places the segment somewhere else either, so the agreement neither covers the segment nor is shown to be breached: the correct finding is undetermined, and because that finding changes the amount, the case goes to a person [F3][RD-5].

The driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed (F11) adds nothing: it is not part of the chat record and a claim of agreement found only in a driver's statement is not consent (G11); the chat record here is complete and fully timestamped (F10), so there is no waiver by unrecorded messaging [F11][F10][RD-5]. The RD-6 flag is not engaged: the driver's 90-day profile shows 4 disputes, 2 upheld and route disputes upheld = 0, and the profile may not decide this case anyway [F18][RD-6]. No separate rider stop is measured in the segment, so RD-3(a) has nothing to exempt [F3][RD-3].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages, the driver's statement and the traffic facts. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the exchange is a route question and an agreement, and the rider's complaint is only about the fare and uncertainty over the road taken (F8, F9, F11, complaint). Nothing to escalate on SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 grounds [F8][F9][SAFE-1].

Evidence: the record settles the segment, the fare and the no-incident screen, but not the identity of the road driven during 21:58–22:05, which RD-5 needs to decide exemption; the fare record F4 ($3.64 = 2.58 km × $1.4098/km) must not be used on its own as the off-route measure because RD-2's formula runs on the non-exempt segment's extra_km per the trace [F3][F4][RD-2]. I therefore cannot rule, and escalate with a factual summary for the reviewer rather than treating the missing path road-name as if it favoured either side.

ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: confirm from the trip path/road records whether the 21:58–22:05 off-route stretch was actually driven on Tampines Avenue 7 (the road the rider agreed to); if it was, close with no refund to the rider; if it was not, refund the non-exempt segment's extra km at the trip rate. Do not apply any account flag on the current record.

proposed_ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (Hougang Mall → Changi Airport T3, total charged $42.25, F7), so a non-exempt off-route segment would feed directly into the fare and be refundable under RD-2 [F7][RD-2]. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists (F3, 21:58–22:05, 4.04 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.90 km, +2.13 km, up to 1209 m off route) and that no RD-4(a) incident supports it: the only traffic records are speed bands (F12 Tampines Expressway band 2 21:33–21:58; F13 Punggol Road band 4; F14 Airport Boulevard band 5) and F15 records no incidents, so RD-4 does not exempt the segment [F3][F12][F15][RD-4].

The open element is consent scope under RD-5. Read in context, the chat is not a general "whichever way is faster" authorisation: the driver asked a specific routing question — “Jam on Tampines Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Tampines Avenue 7?” (F8, 21:55) — and the rider replied specifically, “可以，走 Tampines Avenue 7 吧” (F9, 21:56). The rider's agreement is on its face a SPECIFIC named-road authorisation limited to Tampines Avenue 7, and it was sent before the segment started at 21:58, so a wording that covers the segment exists [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. But RD-5 requires the record to tie the segment to the named road: a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, or a road name in a fact. Nothing does — the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, and the off-route measurement (up to 1209 m from the optimal route) does not itself say which road was used [F3][F9][RD-5]. Timing alone cannot supply the tie (G13). Nothing places the segment somewhere else either, so the agreement neither covers the segment nor is shown to be breached: the correct finding is undetermined, and because that finding changes the amount, the case goes to a person [F3][RD-5].

The driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed (F11) adds nothing: it is not part of the chat record and a claim of agreement found only in a driver's statement is not consent (G11); the chat record here is complete and fully timestamped (F10), so there is no waiver by unrecorded messaging [F11][F10][RD-5]. The RD-6 flag is not engaged: the driver's 90-day profile shows 4 disputes, 2 upheld and route disputes upheld = 0, and the profile may not decide this case anyway [F18][RD-6]. No separate rider stop is measured in the segment, so RD-3(a) has nothing to exempt [F3][RD-3].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages, the driver's statement and the traffic facts. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the exchange is a route question and an agreement, and the rider's complaint is only about the fare and uncertainty over the road taken (F8, F9, F11, complaint). Nothing to escalate on SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 grounds [F8][F9][SAFE-1].

Evidence: the record settles the segment, the fare and the no-incident screen, but not the identity of the road driven during 21:58–22:05, which RD-5 needs to decide exemption; the fare record F4 ($3.64 = 2.58 km × $1.4098/km) must not be used on its own as the off-route measure because RD-2's formula runs on the non-exempt segment's extra_km per the trace [F3][F4][RD-2]. I therefore cannot rule, and escalate with a factual summary for the reviewer rather than treating the missing path road-name as if it favoured either side.

But RD-5 / G13 require a record tying the driven segment to that named road (a stop on it, a message placing the car on it, a road name in a fact); no fact does, and nothing places the segment elsewhere (F3 only measures distance off the optimal route). The agreement's scope over this segment is therefore undetermined, and since it changes the amount the case goes to a human.

proposed_ruling.escalation_reason: Route deviation on a metered RydeTAXI trip: one off-route segment 21:58–22:05 adds 2.13 km (F3) and no RD-4 incident excuses it (F12, F15). The rider agreed before the segment to a specific road, Tampines Avenue 7 (F8, F9), but no record ties the driven segment to that road, so exemption under RD-5 cannot be decided (G13). Human should check the trip's road/path data or driver-recorded route to see whether the car was on Tampines Avenue 7 during 21:58–22:05; if yes, no refund; if no, refund 2.13 km × $1.4098/km = $3.00 under RD-2. ? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 21:58:50 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 21:55 driver: “Jam on Tampines Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Tampines Avenue 7?”; F9: Chat #2 21:56 rider: “可以，走 Tampines Avenue 7 吧。”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I asked the rider before turning off via Tampines Avenue 7 and the rider agreed.” (F8, F9, F11)
